Hippocampal lipidome and transcriptome profile alterations triggered by acute exposure of mice to GSM 1800 MHz mobile phone radiation.

This study provides preliminary evidence that mobile phone radiation induces hippocampal lipidome and transcriptome changes that may explain the brain proteome changes and memory deficits previously shown by our group.

Translation: Evidence was found that exposing mice to 2 hours of cellphone radiation caused a change in their brains.

The observed changes may explain memory loss. More research is needed.

Hippocampus: an important organ inside the brain that is part of the limbic system (memory, emotion, stimulation). It's responsible for short and long-term memory, as well as spatial (3d, location) memory.

Lipidome: lipids = fatty acids, oils. Lipidome = encompassing term of the complex fatty acid structure surrounding all cells.

Transcriptome: transcription = gene transcription = the way the computer program of the DNA runs to transform its information into building blocks for the body inside the cell.

TL;DR: the radiation was found to alter the way the genes in the cells function (gene expression), and also alter it's fatty acid profile. The structure of the lipid (fatty-acid) membrane of the hippocampal cells was altered as a result.

Super TL;DR: radiation was found to change how the cells responsible for memory inside the brain operate.

The group had previously found indications of memory deficits in their mice while testing with radiation, and this is now a more specific indication of why this could be happening.
